title: introduce-temporal-slo-snapshots-and-soft-kill-switch
author: Maya Thompson
description: Motivation: Recent incident (SUP-4421) showed the control plane's abrupt circuit opens caused aggressive KV cache invalidation and a sharp regen spike when regions recovered. Operators need a low-risk operator action to stop accepting new work for a tenant/region while preserving runtime state and enabling a gradual handoff. This PR implements two cooperating features: (1) temporal SLO snapshots: periodic, atomic snapshots of per-tenant SLO state and connection leases that can be used to restore a consistent soft-state after a transient failure, and (2) a soft kill-switch at the routing layer: an operator-facing API/CLI to probabilistically reject new requests for a target scope (tenant/region) with configurable pacing and holdoff semantics so in-flight requests and KV caches are preserved. What this changes: atomic snapshotting of SLO and lease tables into the control plane's ephemeral store; a restore path used by the regional reconciler to fast-reinstate leases without forcing cache flush; routing-level soft-kill with token-bucket based pacing and a TTLed holdoff window that is recorded in the snapshot; new rwctl commands to trigger soft-kill/restore; metrics and tracing hooks for snapshot durations, reject-rate, and restored-lease counts. Implementation notes: snapshots are lightweight (only pointers and compacted SLO deltas) to avoid I/O pressure; we added a two-phase restore (metadata rebind then lease re-announce) to prevent races with the KV cache drainer. The soft kill is implemented as a middleware in the routing stack that consults an in-memory holdoff policy with a probabilistic rejection decision and a warmup cooldown schedule. Operator actions are persisted to the snapshot store so manual soft-kills survive control plane failover. Testing: unit tests for snapshot encoder/decoder, integration test that simulates control plane failover and verifies no mass KV flush, e2e runway (lightweight) that exercises rwctl soft-kill + restore path. Load tests on perf-lab show <2% additional p99 request latency under steady-state. Migration and rollout: feature-flag guarded (enable: controlplane.temporal_slo_snapshot = true). Default off in main; rollout plan is: internal canary -> staged rollout -> org-wide opt-in. Docs and rwctl help updated in this PR. Checklist: [x] Feature flag guarded [x] Unit + integration tests [x] rwctl subcommand and docs [x] Telemetry (metrics + traces) [x] Load validation in perf-lab Related: ENG-1249 (slo drift at failover), ENG-1302 (kv regen storms), SUP-4421 (incident)

review_comments: Arjun Patel: Nice design. Two concerns: race between restore and KV drainer - can you add a guard that delays drainer until metadata rebind completes?

Maya Thompson: Added two-phase restore (metadata rebind -> lease re-announce). See commit a9c3f11. Also added an explicit 'drainer_holdoff' signal in the snapshot store so drainer checks it before flushing.
Leah Kim: Please add Prometheus labels to the reject-rate metric to distinguish tenant vs region and include the feature-flag name in logs for easier triage.
Maya Thompson: Added labels and feature-flag log prefix in 8d2e6b0. Also updated docs to mention metric cardinality tradeoffs.
Diego Rivera: CI showed a flaky test on Mac builders; looks like a timing assumption in snapshot_restore_test.go. Can you make it deterministic?
Maya Thompson: Converted the test to use a deterministic fake clock and bumped the test timeouts. Fix in c4b7ffa.
release_notes: Operator tooling: added rwctl soft-kill/restore commands and a feature-flagged temporal SLO snapshot capability. Enables safe operator pausing of new traffic for tenant/region without mass KV cache invalidation. Rollout controlled by feature flag; see docs/operators/soft_kill_and_snapshots.md for operator guidance.
